facts.detail: Ofcom first published the infrastructure-reports hub on 19 December 2023.
The hub was last updated on 27 May 2026.
The hub covers UK fixed-broadband and mobile-network coverage and performance research.
It identifies Connected Nations as Ofcom's annual communications-infrastructure report.
The hub states that Ofcom also publishes a coverage update and a planned-network-deployment update.
The 2026 planned-network-deployments report is listed in the hub.
The Spring 2026 Connected Nations update is listed in the hub.
Connected Nations 2025 is listed as the annual report for 2025.
The hub retains links to earlier Connected Nations updates and reports.
The report index is retained as source-discovery evidence only and is not promoted as parcel coverage.

guard_streams.write_limit: Nation-level and constituency-level statistics are aggregate geographic evidence and cannot establish present serviceability or speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Nations report 2025 on 19 November 2025.
The publication provides separate broadband and mobile reporting for the UK's nations.
The Scotland report states that 71 percent of residential properties had access to full fibre.
Scotland's full-fibre availability increased by nine percentage points, representing about 250,000 additional premises.
Full-fibre take-up in Scotland is reported at 43 percent, up from 35 percent.
The report estimates around 10,000 Scottish premises could not access decent broadband from fixed-line or fixed wireless networks.
The Wales report states that 78 percent of residential premises had access to full fibre.
Full-fibre take-up in Wales is reported at 49 percent.
The report estimates around 6,000 Welsh premises could not access decent broadband from fixed-line or fixed wireless networks.
The nations publication directs users to the interactive report for area-specific availability data.
